approach:
Hold a job the kill switch stops in planning or at producer start. Do not close it failed. One new method in run/mod.rs, `close_or_hold`, replaces the calls to `close_dispatched` at mod.rs:1349, 1355 and 1376 (`finish_dispatched`). Call 1328 (preflight stop) stays direct. `close_or_hold` is the one shared point, and it works in three steps.

1. `kill_switch_stage(&Closing)` decides whether the closing is a kill-switch stop. The closing's `happened.reason` must contain `kill_switch_stop_reason()`, which is `DriverError::Stopped.to_string()` (athena-agent lib.rs:131). It must also have no candidate, no verification and no Producer invocation in `new_invocations`. So only stops in planning and at producer start qualify. A stop after a producer pass or at the verifier keeps today's failure path. The planner site (planning.rs:179), the critic site (:382) and the producer site (producer.rs:366) already put `{error}` into the reason, so none of them needs an edit.
2. A kill-switch stop goes to `hold_for_kill_switch`, also in mod.rs. It commits the invocations, plans and critiques as a records-only commit with no outcome and no score, the same shape as the disk and slot holds (close.rs:226-228). Baseline, candidate and verification are left out, so a resume re-runs them without rewriting a record. It then writes a state-dir marker `KillHold { stage, prediction }` (new in state.rs), and returns an error so `go` fails as it does for any hold. With no files to commit it writes only the marker. The job stays Dispatched with no outcome, so no failure count, score, introspection or scope-guard attempt sees it.
3. Status shows the marked job as `stopped`. `status()` counts it under `stopped`, not under `failed` or `interrupted`. It is left out of the first-round "plan stopped" count.

Resume runs in place. `go_job`'s Dispatched arm (mod.rs:477) checks the marker first. `dispatch` gains a `held: Option<KillHold>` parameter (the Proposed arm and the reread recursion pass `None`). For a held job it reuses the committed Job record and the stored prediction commit and commits no second Dispatch. It reads the stored `brief-producer.md` from the prediction commit, and it takes the accepted reading from `job.readings` by `Job.accepted_reading`, so no reader runs. If the last critique accepted, planning is skipped and the kept plan and critique are pushed into `closing`. The verifier and the producer read `closing.plans.last()`, and the identical re-added records are no-ops in the commit. If the last critique was a revise, planning continues from round N+1, seeded from that plan and its findings; this needs a new `from_round` parameter on `plan_round`. If there is no critique, planning starts at round 1. An in-flight planner or critic call is re-run, and an unreviewed plan is not kept, because re-running would collide with the `job-plan-N.json` path (athena-data records.rs:1388).

`Athena::start_with` (manage.rs:511) gains one call, `resume_kill_stopped(ui)`, between `registry().start()` and `run_pending_introspections`. It resumes every marked job through `go_with_stages` and never fails the start: it prints a line per problem and stops if the switch comes on again. A job whose reading config hash changed, a pinned job, or a job whose prediction commit is gone cannot resume in place. Its marker is cleared, so it reads `interrupted` and `athena retry <id>` handles it. That is the only case where a reader runs, and it is the user's explicit command.

No OutcomeState or JobState variant is added, so no serialized record changes. Non-kill-switch failures keep `failure()` (mod.rs:2491) and `close_dispatched`. `failure()` prints the word `stopped` instead of `failed` only when the reason carries the kill-switch text, so the user does not see a misleading `failed` line before `held`.

Files outside the brief's list:
- producer.rs and close.rs from the previous plan are dropped. The design needs neither. `commit_hold` and `push_closing_records` are private to close.rs, so the hold builds its own three record loops in mod.rs.
- manage.rs stays, as a one-line edit. Criterion 3 names `start_with`, which is defined at manage.rs:511, and no listed file can host that call.
- lib.rs and commands.rs from the list are left untouched. `state`, `status` and `run` are already `pub mod` (lib.rs:153,160,161), and `start_with(&Terminal)` (commands.rs:673) already prints the resume lines through the Ui.

decisions.choice: The shared stop point is `close_or_hold` in run/mod.rs. It recognises a kill-switch stop by `kill_switch_stop_reason()`, a function that returns `DriverError::Stopped.to_string()`.
decisions.reason: All three stop sites build their reason from `{error}`, whose Display is the typed variant's text. One derived function (no literal copy) and one consumer give a single place to Grep for. It needs no edit to producer.rs or close.rs, which are outside the deliverables. The extra conditions (no candidate, no verification, no Producer invocation) keep a stop after a producer pass or at the verifier on the existing failure path.

rejected.option: A typed flag on `Closing` set at each site
rejected.why: The producer site is in producer.rs, which is outside the deliverables. It would also leave two detection mechanisms.
close.rs is outside the deliverables, and `commit_hold` there is private anyway.

rejected.option: Close the job failed with an environment-style reason
rejected.why: It would still count as `failed` in status. A closed job cannot be resumed in place: go_job bails on Closed at mod.rs:496, and `athena retry` runs the reader.

decisions.choice: The hold is a records-only commit (invocations, plans, critiques) plus a state-dir marker `KillHold { stage, prediction }`. The job stays Dispatched and shows as `stopped` in status. Meaning of the marker, quoted from introspect.rs:1312-1314: "kept in the pending queue (no record, no failed status) ... `athena start` runs the queue". The job version adds a committed hold commit and an in-place resume. `Job.accepted_reading` and `Job.accepted_by` (athena-data records.rs:644-645, set at dispatch from `reading.n` at mod.rs:1235) are read, never changed.
decisions.reason: A Dispatched job with no outcome is already invisible to failure, introspection and scope-guard counts, as the disk hold is (close.rs:170-175). The invocation records keep the cost accounting. The marker follows the introspection pending-queue pattern (state.rs:89) and the disk hold marker (state.rs:330). The display name `stopped` is a status string only (status.rs:1092-1098), not a stored value. It is distinct from `FirstRoundCounts.stopped` (status/planning.rs:8-11), which counts a different thing.

rejected.why: OutcomeState is in athena-data, outside the deliverables. It is a serialized record change needing round-trip and gate coverage.

rejected.option: Commit nothing at the stop and keep everything in the state dir
rejected.why: It would lose the invocation cost records and the kept plan, which the criteria say are kept.

decisions.choice: Resume in place through `go_job` and `dispatch(held)`. It reuses the Job record and the prediction commit stored in the marker, reads the stored brief, takes the accepted reading from `job.readings`, and skips planning when the last critique accepted.
decisions.reason: `dispatch` takes a reading and starts no reader (mod.rs:1015-1067). The Job record and brief are already committed, and rewriting them would modify committed records. Reusing the stored brief keeps the prompt equal to what was committed.

rejected.why: It starts a new job and runs `ask`, so the reader runs (reading.rs:1262-1319). That fails criterion 3.

rejected.option: Commit a second Dispatch commit for the same job
rejected.why: It rewrites the committed job.json and moves the base.

decisions.choice: Completed planning rounds are kept. An in-flight planner or critic call is re-run, and an unreviewed plan (critic stopped before its critique) is not kept. A last critique that is a revise continues at round N+1, seeded from that plan and its findings. `plan_round` gets a `from_round` parameter, clamped to `max_rounds`.
decisions.reason: Plan and critique record paths are keyed by round (records.rs:1388-1389). Re-planning round N over a kept `job-plan-N.json` would modify a committed record. The loop at planning.rs:44 starts at round 1 today.

rejected.option: Keep the unreviewed plan by pushing it into `closing.plans` at the critic site
rejected.why: The re-run's round numbering would collide with it, or the plan would have to be reviewed without a critic call.

decisions.choice: `athena start` resumes held jobs synchronously from `start_with`, the way it already runs pending introspections (manage.rs:513). A job that cannot resume in place has its marker cleared and falls back to `interrupted` and `athena retry`.
decisions.reason: Criterion 3 names `start_with`. A changed reading config (mod.rs:1030) must reread, and the reader running there is the existing rule. This settles the previous plan's open question in code, so no question remains.

rejected.option: Resume only on a later `athena go` or drain
rejected.why: The held job would not resume after `athena start`, which the request asks for. A drain would also treat it as interrupted and retry it with a reader (steward.rs:450).

rejected.option: Silently dispatch with the new config
rejected.why: The reading was made under the old config. That is what the existing reread rule prevents.

decisions.choice: In status, `state_name` returns `stopped` for a marked, not-running Dispatched job. `scan_jobs` leaves it out of the first-round `stopped` count but still counts an accepted first round. It sets no `JobLine.hold` text.
decisions.reason: A round-1 revise followed by a round-2 stop would otherwise count as a plan stopped in round 1 (status.rs:1126-1130 uses the last critique's round). A `hold` text would render as "(still queued)" (display.rs:1074).

rejected.why: The stopped job would show as `interrupted` and could be counted as a first-round stop. Criterion 4 forbids this.

risks.risk: The resume re-adds the kept plan and critique (when planning is skipped) through `push_closing_records`, which rewrites existing record paths. If their bytes are not identical, the gate could see a modified record.
risks.mitigation: The gate requires committed records to round-trip, so the bytes are identical and git sees no change. The kill_switch_hold_resume tests run the real `commit_records` gate and fail if it refuses. If they do, the fix is to skip the kept records when building the closing files.

risks.risk: The hold commit or the marker write fails after the switch fires.
risks.mitigation: A failed commit returns the error with the job id (as close.rs:229-232 does), writes no marker, and leaves the job Dispatched, shown as `interrupted`, so `athena retry` still works. A marker write failure is reported on the held line.

risks.risk: Detection by reason text could hold a stop that is not a planning or producer-start stop.
risks.mitigation: `kill_switch_stage` also requires no candidate, no verification and no Producer invocation in the closing. Stops in a producer send-back or at the verifier keep the failure path. Test (ii) of criterion 5 and the existing lifecycle test at lifecycle.rs:1240 (a producer killed mid-run closes `killed`) cover the boundary.

risks.risk: `athena start` now runs jobs and can take long or spend money.
risks.mitigation: This matches the introspection queue, which also runs model calls inside `start_with`. The resume loop stops if the switch comes on again, and every problem is a line, never a failed start. The job lock keeps another process from running the same job.

risks.risk: After a long stop the branch has moved or the config changed. The resumed job uses its old prediction commit as base.
risks.mitigation: A config hash mismatch, a pinned job, or a missing prediction commit clears the marker and falls back to `athena retry`. A moved branch goes through the existing stale landing path, and the test fixture does not move the branch.

risks.risk: A resumed job with `from_round` greater than `max_rounds` would reach the `unreachable!` at planning.rs:78.
risks.mitigation: `plan_round` clamps `from_round` to `max_rounds`. A revise in the last round already stops the job, so it is never held with such a state.

risks.risk: The producer's decision gate requires reconciling the decisions that govern run/ files.
risks.mitigation: The appended docs/decisions.md entry is the reconciliation. The producer reads the governing decisions through the prompt before editing.

demonstrations.method: The tests of criteria 1 and 2 go on to call `athena.start_with(&Lines::default())`. The wrapper's `fired` flag keeps it from stopping again. Each test reads its own wrapper's Reader counter before the stop and after the resume.
demonstrations.observes: `start_with` returns true. The job reaches `JobState::Closed(OutcomeState::Landed)`. The marker is gone. The Reader count is unchanged by the resume (one, from `ask`). In the producer-stop test the Planner and Critic counts are also unchanged (planning skipped). In test A the planner runs again once. In test B it runs once more at round 2, with `job-plan-2` and `critique-2` added.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the `start_with` resume (manage.rs call and `go_job` marker branch), the job stays Dispatched and the Closed assertion fails. If resume went through `athena retry`, the Reader count would rise.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point `Athena::start_with` (manage.rs:511), which calls the new `resume_kill_stopped`, then `go_with_stages`, `go_job` and `dispatch(held)`. Fake: the counting wrapper over `planning_script`, injected through `athena_with`. `start_with` exists. The resume code is added by steps 5 to 7. The commit path is the real `commit_records`, so the gate checks the kept-plan re-add.

demonstrations.method: After each hold (tests A, B and the producer stop), call `athena.status()` (status.rs:1188), which runs `scan_jobs` (:1114) over `Records::load_current`. This follows the pattern at tests.rs:4755.
demonstrations.observes: `jobs_by_state` has `stopped` = 1 and no `failed` or `interrupted`. The job is in `open` with state `stopped` and `hold` None. `status.planning` has `stopped` = 0 in test B, where a round-1 revise critique exists. The `next` lines include an `athena start` line for the job.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the held job were counted `failed` or `interrupted`, or as a first-round plan stop, the `jobs_by_state` and `planning.stopped` assertions fail. Without the `stopped` arm in `state_name` the job reads `interrupted`.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point `Athena::status` (public, status.rs:1188), which calls the private `scan_jobs`. No visibility change is needed. Records come from the real committed hold. Exists, and the fixture is the one of criterion 1.

demonstrations.method: Two runs with the stop file never written. (i) The wrapper makes the Planner turn non-Success, as the existing planner-failure tests do (tests.rs:1878-2079). (ii) The wrapper makes the Producer turn non-Success. Both then call `athena.status()`. The whole `cargo test --locked` run covers all existing tests.
demonstrations.observes: Each returns `Finished` with `OutcomeState::Failed`. No marker exists. `jobs_by_state["failed"]` is 1. The `failed     ` line is printed, not `stopped`.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the hold caught every `could not run` stop or every failure, these jobs would stay Dispatched with a marker, and the Failed and count assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point `Athena::go`, with the wrapper over `base_script` (tests.rs:224) injected through `athena_with`. A FakeTurn with a non-Success `outcome` (fake.rs:17). Exists.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff. `kill_switch_stop_reason` is defined once. `kill_switch_stage` and `close_or_hold` are the only consumers that lead to the hold. `close_or_hold` is called at the three sites that formerly called `close_dispatched` (mod.rs:1349, 1355 and `finish_dispatched`). `hold_for_kill_switch` is called only from `close_or_hold`. No kill-switch literal is added, because the reason comes from `DriverError::Stopped.to_string()`. The diff touches neither producer.rs nor close.rs.
demonstrations.observes: One definition, one decision point, one hold function, the planning and producer-start stops reaching it through the same call.

demonstrations.method: Read the stat and the docs/decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md hunks.
demonstrations.observes: Only the files named in this plan appear. docs/decisions.md has only added lines: a new entry whose Provenance bullet cites job 20261030-060410-mavp as the introspection counterpart, and no existing entry edited. CHANGELOG.md has a new Unreleased entry. Nothing under records/, athena.toml, defaults.toml or .github/workflows changed.

demonstrations.method: On the final tree run `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`, each as its own cargo command. The test run covers the new run/tests.rs tests, the new state.rs round-trip test and the new introspection.rs test. It also covers every existing suite that reads the changed code: status, drain, retry and introspection (athena-cli/tests/drain.rs and lifecycle.rs), plus the xtask policy tests and the `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` test.
demonstrations.fails_without: A formatting or lint error in the new code, or any existing test broken by the changed `dispatch`, `failure()`, `scan_jobs` or `start_with`, fails the checks.
demonstrations.seam: The entry points are the production functions the suites call: `Athena::go`, `Athena::start_with` and `Athena::status`. The fixtures are the existing `FakeAgentDriver` scripts via `athena_with` (tests.rs:191), the `check_seam` (mod.rs:1518) and the introspection.rs `setup` harness (introspection.rs:1541). Nothing new is injected for this criterion. All exist today, and the new tests join them in steps 8 and 9.
